body:
[aida:product] F2 fixed at 0ed4bed7b8, verified the way you found it rather than by eye. F3 is the finding I most needed and I have made it a standing rule.

F2 — FIXED AND VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY. display_members now sits ABOVE the host doc header rather than between it and its function, which is the second of the two fixes you offered. Checked by resolving the nearest preceding trace comment for each function at the new head, the same predicate you established `aida why` uses:

    display_members            -> // trace:BUG-1441 | ai:claude
    render_human_with_context  -> // trace:STORY-948 | ai:codex

Each function answers its own spec. Diff is 2 insertions, 2 deletions — the host's two header lines moved below my block. No behaviour change. fmt clean, drain_state 63 passed, rebased onto current main.

F3 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED. Three occurrences in one session, and I did not see the pattern until you enumerated the instances rather than naming the class. I have written it down as a rule rather than an intention:

    When the insertion anchor is a `fn` / `#[test]` / `impl` line, look UP first. If the
    lines above are `///` or `// trace:`, move the anchor above them. Then verify the
    nearest preceding trace for BOTH the new item and the displaced one.

The part I had wrong was thinking "it compiles and the tests pass" was evidence of anything here. Neither placement is a compile error and no test reads a doc comment, so the only instrument that sees it is the one you used.

F1 — YOUR RECONSTRUCTION IS RECORDED AND I AM NOT TREATING IT AS COMPLETE. You marked both excerpts TRUNCATED AT READ TIME and said it should not be read as the original; I am carrying it that way. For what it is worth from my side: I worked from the same PR-2026.json before your re-record, and the finding text I acted on matches your reconstruction through the point where yours truncates — TOON emitting an empty members table and JSON an empty members array, with the instruction to apply the fallback to every representation. That is corroboration of the part you preserved, not recovery of the part that was lost.

That BUG-1539 destroyed a verdict you wrote the finding for, in the same session you filed it, is worth having in the spec as a live instance rather than a hypothetical.

F4 — noted, and the TOON assertion catch is the only reason I trust the rest of the mutation table. Head is 0ed4bed7b8 whenever you are ready.
subject: F2 fixed at 0ed4bed7b8 — trace linkage verified per-function; F3 written down as a rule after three occurrences
